items.title: Gemini Decisions API
items.summary: Gemini Decisions API Google join Jev and OpenAI in the decision model category with "Gemini Decision 1". This new model API is almost identical to Jev: it supports the same three types of questions (yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring) and even reuses Jev's term "Noul" for a yes/no question. It's priced the same as the GPT-6 Luna decision model: 10 cents per million input tokens, and output is free. Jev remains the cheapest of the three, at 4.2 cents per million. Jev is text (and JSON) only. OpenAI can handle text and images. Gemini Decision 1 is fully multi-model: it covers text, images, audio, video, and PDFs. I tested it against video by passing these questions to it along with my Yonkers stomping robot video file: dragon: Does this video have a dragon in it? robot: Does this video have a robot in it? france: Is this video set in France? usa: Is this video set in the USA? Jev and OpenAI both return 1.0 or 0.0 for yes/no questions, but Gemini insists on being a little less confident than that: { "dragon" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.04976021841520312 }, "robot" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.9234055387792485 }, "france" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.08329171353166241 }, "usa" : { "type" : " yes_no " , "probability" : 0.9230459995157706 } } Via Hacker News Tags: ai , generative-ai , gemini , llm-release , jev , decision-models

items.summary: aws-emulator Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so. It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog. It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great if you could download a single binary and use that as part of a standard test suite in other languages and on other platforms. items.title: llm 0.37.2
items.summary: Release: llm 0.37.2 Fixes a security issue reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w . LLM has a mechanism called extra-openai-models.yaml - now managed by the new-in-0.37 llm openai endpoint add command - for using LLM with OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. Daniel reported two ways this could accidentally send your configured OpenAI API key to one of those providers: if the key named by api_key_name had never been stored, or if a responses: true model was run with -o chat_completions 1 . Tags: projects , security , llm , releases

items.title: Anthropic's IPO roadshow video
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO roadshow video Anthropic kicked off their IPO roadshow yesterday, and their roadshow video has some previously unreleased information about how their business works. The section on "Approach to compute" with co-founder Tom Brown is particularly interesting, describing how Anthropic train and serve Claude across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs. I'm not sure why there's no official video transcript, but here's one that I extracted using MacWhisper. Highlights below: We train and serve Claude now across all four major chip families. That's only possible because early on we made an unconventional bet on a multi-chip strategy. At the time, many people thought that running AI models on different chips wasn't worth the effort. Each chip needs its own tailored software stack and inference stack, which is expensive and difficult to build. We've now been doing it for years, and we've gotten incredibly good at it. [...] As an example, this year, we started working with AMD GPUs for the first time. In the past, bringing on a new chip platform took dozens of engineers months of work This time, we had Mythos try it out. It got Claude running on AMD in just three days, with basically no human intervention . Claude ported or wrote almost 100% of the kernels. [...] The second driver of our compute advantage is our rate of discovery of compute multipliers. We focus on total effective compute, which is the multiplicative product of physical capacity times the compute multipliers that we discover. Each one we discover makes our pool of total effective compute bigger. For example, say you need 100 units of compute to train a model of a certain intelligence. it.title: Agenti AI che collaborano: Cisco discute di Scope, Accord e Concord
it.summary: In questo episodio, Vijoy Pandey di Cisco affronta le sfide dei sistemi multi-agente. Vengono presentati protocolli open-source come Scope, Accord e Concord per coordinare flussi di lavoro autonomi.
it.why_it_matters: I protocolli aperti mirano a risolvere i problemi di coordinamento tra diversi sistemi di intelligenza artificiale, facilitando l'allineamento semantico e la negoziazione degli intenti.
it.extended_analysis:
Il panorama dell'intelligenza artificiale si sta evolvendo verso ecosistemi in cui più agenti autonomi devono operare congiuntamente. Tuttavia, far comunicare e collaborare questi sistemi presenta notevoli complessità tecniche.

Nel corso dell'episodio, l'approfondimento si concentra su come i protocolli open-source Scope, Accord e Concord cerchino di affrontare tali ostacoli, offrendo un quadro per l'allineamento semantico e la gestione degli intenti nei flussi di lavoro distribuiti.

Gli ascoltatori possono approfondire le dinamiche di progettazione dei sistemi multi-agente e le soluzioni proposte per abilitare una cooperazione efficace tra intelligenze artificiali autonome.
it.context: La discussione si inserisce nel contesto della crescente adozione di agenti intelligenti autonomi e della necessità di standard aperti per evitare ecosistemi frammentati e proprietari.

en.title: AI Agents That Think Together: Cisco's Vijoy Pandey on Multi-Agent Systems
en.summary: Vijoy Pandey of Cisco discusses multi-agent AI challenges and explores how open-source protocols like Scope, Accord, and Concord enable collaboration and semantic alignment across autonomous workflows.
en.why_it_matters: Open protocols are essential for overcoming coordination hurdles between distinct AI systems, enabling seamless intent negotiation and structured collaboration across autonomous workflows.
en.extended_analysis:
As artificial intelligence shifts from standalone models to interconnected multi-agent ecosystems, managing how different systems cooperate becomes a core architectural challenge. Without unified standards, autonomous agents risk operating in silos.

This episode examines how open-source frameworks such as Scope, Accord, and Concord attempt to address semantic alignment and intent negotiation. By establishing shared protocols, these systems aim to foster more reliable cooperation in complex environments.

Listeners will gain insights into the current engineering approaches designed to make multi-agent collaboration practical and scalable for modern technical infrastructures.
en.context: This discussion addresses the broader industry transition toward collaborative autonomous workflows and the growing demand for interoperable standards in AI development.
key_takeaways: Key challenges in scaling multi-agent AI architectures.
Overview of open-source protocols Scope, Accord, and Concord.
Methods for achieving semantic alignment and intent negotiation.
highlights: Featured guest: Vijoy Pandey, SVP and GM of Outshift by Cisco.
Exploration of open-source protocols for autonomous agent workflows.

es.why_it_matters: Los protocolos abiertos buscan resolver los problemas de coordinación entre inteligencias artificiales, mejorando la negociación de intenciones y la alineación semántica.
es.extended_analysis:
A medida que la inteligencia artificial evoluciona hacia arquitecturas multi-agente, la capacidad de distintos sistemas autónomos para cooperar de forma fluida se vuelve crucial. La falta de estándares comunes puede limitar la interoperabilidad.

En este episodio se examinan las propuestas técnicas que utilizan protocolos abiertos como Scope, Accord y Concord para estructurar la colaboración y el alineamiento semántico entre flujos de trabajo automatizados.

Los oyentes pueden conocer las perspectivas de la industria sobre cómo abordar la complejidad operativa de los agentes de IA distribuidos.
es.context: El debate refleja la atención actual sobre la interoperabilidad y el diseño de protocolos abiertos para gestionar sistemas de IA autónomos a gran escala.
key_takeaways: Retos en la colaboración de sistemas multi-agente.

de.title: Kooperierende KI-Agenten: Cisco über semantische Ausrichtung und Protokolle
de.summary: Vijoy Pandey von Cisco erörtert die Herausforderungen von Multi-Agenten-Systemen und erklärt, wie offene Protokolle wie Scope, Accord und Concord die Zusammenarbeit in autonomen Arbeitsabläufen ermöglichen.
de.why_it_matters: Offene Protokolle adressieren Koordinationsprobleme zwischen verschiedenen KI-Systemen und erleichtern die semantische Ausrichtung sowie die Intentionsaushandlung.
de.extended_analysis:
Der Übergang zu verteilten Multi-Agenten-Systemen stellt die Softwarearchitektur vor neue Herausforderungen, da autonome KI-Einheiten verlässlich miteinander kommunizieren und kooperieren müssen.

In dieser Episode wird beleuchtet, wie Open-Source-Protokolle wie Scope, Accord und Concord dazu beitragen können, semantische Konsistenz und strukturierte Intentionsaushandlung in komplexen Workflows zu gewährleisten.

Hörer erhalten Einblicke in aktuelle architektonische Lösungsansätze zur Bewältigung der Interoperabilität zwischen autonomen Agenten.
de.context: Die Diskussion spiegelt die technische Entwicklung hin zu vernetzten, autonomen KI-Workflows und den Bedarf an standardisierten Kommunikationsprotokollen wider.
key_takeaways: Herausforderungen bei der Skalierung von Multi-Agenten-Architekturen.
Bedeutung offener Protokolle wie Scope, Accord und Concord.
Ansätze für semantische Ausrichtung und Intentionsaushandlung.
highlights: Gast: Vijoy Pandey, SVP und GM von Outshift by Cisco.
Fokus auf Open-Source-Protokolle für autonome Agenten-Workflows.

items.summary: swyx had already connected Cloudflare email. Then a coding agent opened a pull request that quietly chose Resend for him. Zeno Rocha, Resend’s founder and CEO, explains what answer engine optimization (AEO) looks like from the receiving end of that rec...
items.podcastDescription: Deep dive tecnici con chi costruisce modelli, agenti e infrastrutture AI.

it.title: Progettare per gli agenti AI: la prospettiva di Zeno Rocha su Resend
it.summary: In questo episodio di Latent Space, Zeno Rocha, fondatore e CEO di Resend, racconta come i coding agent scelgano autonomamente i servizi analizzando i flussi di lavoro. Attraverso il caso in cui un agente ha scelto Resend per una pull request, l'episodio esplora l'ottimizzazione per i motori di risposta.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere come gli agenti autonomi prendano decisioni tecniche al posto degli sviluppatori ridefinisce le strategie di visibilità e adozione dei prodotti software.
it.extended_analysis:
Il panorama dello sviluppo software sta cambiando rapidamente con l'introduzione di agenti di codifica autonomi capaci di compiere scelte tecniche in autonomia, come l'integrazione di servizi di posta elettronica. Zeno Rocha offre una prospettiva privilegiata su questo fenomeno, analizzando cosa significhi trovarsi dal lato ricevente di una raccomandazione generata da un'intelligenza artificiale.

L'episodio approfondisce il concetto di answer engine optimization (AEO) e il suo impatto sulle aziende tecnologiche. Quando i software non si rivolgono più solo agli utenti umani ma dialogano direttamente con gli agenti, le dinamiche di mercato e di branding subiscono una trasformazione radicale.
it.context: La discussione si inserisce nel contesto dell'evoluzione degli strumenti di intelligenza artificiale per gli sviluppatori, dove gli agenti autonomi passano dall'essere semplici assistenti a veri e propri decisori operativi nei flussi di lavoro.
key_takeaways: I coding agent possono scegliere autonomamente i servizi software durante la scrittura del codice.
Zeno Rocha spiega l'ottimizzazione per i motori di risposta (AEO) dal punto di vista di un'azienda.
Il ruolo degli strumenti di sviluppo si sposta dall'interazione umana a quella guidata dagli agenti.
highlights: Ospite: Zeno Rocha, fondatore e CEO di Resend.
Conduttore: swyx, che condivide l'esperienza pratica con gli agenti di codifica.

en.title: Designing for Agents: Zeno Rocha on Resend and Autonomous Software
en.summary: In this Latent Space episode, Resend founder and CEO Zeno Rocha discusses how coding agents autonomously choose services. Prompted by an event where an agent quietly selected Resend via a pull request, the conversation explores answer engine optimization from the receiving end.
en.why_it_matters: As coding agents increasingly make independent architectural choices, understanding how software is discovered and selected by AI shifts product strategy entirely.
en.extended_analysis:
The intersection of autonomous agents and developer tooling is creating new paradigms for how software is adopted. When swyx connected Cloudflare email and a coding agent subsequently opened a pull request selecting Resend, it highlighted a shift in how technical products gain traction.

Zeno Rocha breaks down the mechanics of this shift, discussing answer engine optimization (AEO) and what it means for infrastructure companies when AI agents become the primary decision-makers. This episode offers a look into the future where software is built for both human developers and autonomous coding systems.
en.context: The episode reflects the growing trend of AI coding agents executing complex workflows and making automated architectural decisions on behalf of developers.
key_takeaways: Coding agents can independently select backend services based on project context.
Answer engine optimization (AEO) redefines how developer tools gain visibility.
Resend CEO Zeno Rocha shares insights from receiving an AI-driven service selection.
highlights: Featured guest: Zeno Rocha, founder and CEO of Resend.
Context driven by swyx's real-world coding agent experience.

es.title: Diseñando para agentes: Zeno Rocha sobre Resend y el software autónomo
es.summary: En este episodio de Latent Space, Zeno Rocha, fundador y CEO de Resend, analiza cómo los agentes de código eligen servicios de forma autónoma. A partir de una pull request donde un agente seleccionó Resend, se examina la optimización para motores de respuesta.
es.why_it_matters: A medida que los agentes de programación toman decisiones técnicas independientes, comprender cómo las IA descubren el software redefine las estrategias comerciales.
es.extended_analysis:
El desarrollo de software se enfrenta a un cambio de paradigma en el que los agentes autónomos de código ya no solo ayudan, sino que toman decisiones activas sobre qué servicios integrar en los flujos de trabajo de los desarrolladores.

Zeno Rocha examina este fenómeno desde la perspectiva empresarial, analizando la optimización para motores de respuesta (AEO) y cómo las herramientas tecnológicas deben adaptarse a un ecosistema donde los clientes son sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
es.context: La charla aborda el impacto de los agentes de codificación autónomos en la infraestructura moderna y la adopción de software.
key_takeaways: Los agentes de código pueden seleccionar servicios tecnológicos de forma autónoma.
Zeno Rocha analiza el concepto de AEO desde el lado receptor.
Se examinan los cambios en la adopción de herramientas para desarrolladores.
highlights: Invitado: Zeno Rocha, fundador y CEO de Resend.
Presentado por swyx en Latent Space.

zh-CN.why_it_matters: 随着编码代理逐渐代替开发者做出独立的架构选择，理解人工智能如何发现并采用软件已成为产品战略的核心。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
自主编码代理正在重塑软件开发的格局。当人工智能代理在工作流中自主选择后端服务时，技术产品的推广和获客方式也发生了深刻变化。

Zeno Rocha 分享了作为服务提供商如何看待这一趋势，探讨了回答引擎优化（AEO）的概念以及当 AI 成为决策者时对基础设施企业的影响。
zh-CN.context: 本期节目聚焦于人工智能编码代理在实际开发中的表现，以及它们如何改变软件工具的评估和采用流程。

de.why_it_matters: Wenn autonome Agenten eigenständig technische Entscheidungen treffen, verändert dies grundlegend, wie Softwareprodukte entdeckt und in Entwickler-Workflows integriert werden.

Die zunehmende Verbreitung autonomer Coding-Agenten verändert die Art und Weise, wie Software-Infrastrukturen ausgewählt werden. Wenn Agenten eigenständig Dienste wie Resend in Pull Requests einbinden, stehen Anbieter vor neuen Herausforderungen.

Zeno Rocha analysiert dieses Phänomen aus der Praxis und beleuchtet, was Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) für Technologieunternehmen bedeutet, wenn KI-Systeme zu aktiven Entscheidungsträgern werden.

it.title: Decodificare i modelli linguistici: Curt Tigges su interpretabilità e basis
it.summary: In questo episodio di The Cognitive Revolution, il conduttore esplora con Curt Tigges di Goodfire la ricerca sul paper "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis". L'intervista approfondisce l'interpretabilità agentica, la monosemanticità e il reverse engineering dei modelli.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere come i singoli neuroni e le basi interpretabili operino all'interno dei grandi modelli linguistici è cruciale per demistificare il loro funzionamento interno e avanzare verso sistemi più trasparenti.
it.extended_analysis:
L'episodio vede come ospite Curt Tigges, membro dello staff tecnico di Goodfire e coautore insieme a Nick Cammarata del nuovo paper "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis". Questo lavoro si presenta come la controparte più accademica e focalizzata sui modelli linguistici rispetto alle recenti pubblicazioni di Cammarata.

La discussione si muove attorno ai concetti chiave di interpretabilità agentica, monosemanticità e reverse engineering dei sistemi di intelligenza artificiale. Attraverso il dialogo, emergono i tentativi di decodificare il funzionamento profondo dei modelli complessi, offrendo spunti tecnici di rilievo per ricercatori e addetti ai lavori.
it.context: Il dibattito sull'interpretabilità dei modelli di intelligenza artificiale mira a superare la natura di "scatola nera" dei sistemi attuali. Ricerche come quella discussa nel podcast cercano di mappare le rappresentazioni interne dei modelli per renderli più comprensibili.
key_takeaways: Presentazione del paper "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis" di Curt Tigges e Nick Cammarata.
Analisi dei concetti di interpretabilità agentica e monosemanticità nei modelli linguistici.
Discussione sulle tecniche di reverse engineering applicate ai sistemi di IA.
highlights: Ospite dell'episodio è Curt Tigges, membro dello staff tecnico di Goodfire.
Il paper discusso è il compagno più accademico e orientato ai LLM dei recenti lavori di Nick Cammarata.

en.title: Decoding Language Models: Curt Tigges on Agentic Interp and Monosemanticity
en.summary: In this episode of The Cognitive Revolution, host speaks with Curt Tigges of Goodfire about the new paper, "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis." The conversation explores agentic interpretability, monosemanticity, and reverse engineering.
en.why_it_matters: Understanding the internal representations of large language models is essential for moving beyond black-box systems and achieving greater transparency in artificial intelligence.
en.extended_analysis:
The episode features Curt Tigges, a member of the technical staff at Goodfire and co-author alongside Nick Cammarata of the paper "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis." This work serves as the more academic and LLM-focused companion to recent publications by Cammarata.

The discussion centers on agentic interpretability, monosemanticity, and the reverse engineering of complex systems. By examining how individual neurons function as an interpretable basis, the conversation sheds light on ongoing efforts to map and comprehend the internal machinery of modern language models.
en.context: The field of mechanistic interpretability focuses on reverse engineering neural networks to understand how specific internal components drive model behavior, addressing safety and transparency concerns.
key_takeaways: Exploration of the research paper "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis."
Insights into agentic interpretability and monosemanticity in large language models.
Discussion on reverse engineering techniques for neural networks.
highlights: Guest Curt Tigges is a technical staff member at Goodfire.
The paper is co-authored by Curt Tigges and Nick Cammarata.

es.title: Descodificando modelos: Curt Tigges sobre interpretabilidad y monosemia

es.why_it_matters: Comprender los mecanismos internos de los grandes modelos de lenguaje es fundamental para superar el enfoque de caja negra y lograr una mayor transparencia en la inteligencia artificial.
es.extended_analysis:
El episodio cuenta con Curt Tigges, miembro del equipo técnico de Goodfire y coautor junto a Nick Cammarata del trabajo "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis". Este documento actúa como el compañero más académico y enfocado en modelos de lenguaje de las publicaciones recientes de Cammarata.

Durante la entrevista, se examinan conceptos avanzados como la interpretabilidad agéntica, la monosemia y los métodos de ingeniería inversa. La conversación ofrece una perspectiva técnica sobre cómo los investigadores intentan desentrañar las representaciones internas de las redes neuronales.
es.context: La interpretabilidad en la inteligencia artificial busca desglosar el funcionamiento interno de los modelos complejos para examinar cómo procesan la información y toman decisiones.
key_takeaways: Revisión del artículo de investigación "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis".
Análisis de la interpretabilidad agéntica y la monosemia en modelos lingüísticos.
Enfoque en técnicas de ingeniería inversa para sistemas de IA.

El artículo discutido fue coescrito por Curt Tigges y Nick Cammarata.

zh-CN.title: 解码语言模型：Curt Tigges谈智能体可解释性与单义性
zh-CN.summary: 在本期《The Cognitive Revolution》中，主持人与Goodfire技术人员Curt Tigges探讨了新论文《Neurons as an Interpretable Basis》。讨论深入审视了智能体可解释性、单义性以及模型逆向工程。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 理解大型语言模型的内部表征对于打破黑盒系统、实现更高水平的AI透明度具有重要意义。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
本期节目邀请了Goodfire技术人员Curt Tigges作为嘉宾，他与Nick Cammarata共同撰写了新论文《Neurons as an Interpretable Basis》。该论文是Nick近期作品中更具学术性、更聚焦大语言模型的配套研究。

对话围绕智能体可解释性、单义性以及人工智能系统的逆向工程展开。通过探讨神经元如何作为可解释的基础发挥作用，节目展现了研究人员在揭示复杂模型内部机制方面的最新进展。
zh-CN.context: 机制可解释性研究致力于对神经网络进行逆向工程，以便厘清模型内部组件如何协同工作，从而提升人工智能的可靠性与透明度。
key_takeaways: 深入解析研究论文《Neurons as an Interpretable Basis》。
探讨大型语言模型中的智能体可解释性与单义性概念。
审视面向神经网络的逆向工程方法与技术应用。

de.title: Sprachmodelle entschlüsseln: Curt Tigges über Interpretierbarkeit

de.why_it_matters: Die Entschlüsselung der internen Repräsentationen großer Sprachmodelle ist entscheidend, um Black-Box-Systeme besser zu verstehen und die Transparenz in der künstlichen Intelligenz zu erhöhen.

de.context: Die mechanistische Interpretierbarkeit zielt darauf ab, neuronale Netze zu analysieren, um nachzuvollziehen, wie spezifische interne Strukturen das Verhalten von KI-Modellen steuern.

it.why_it_matters: Comprendere il funzionamento interno dei modelli linguistici è cruciale per la trasparenza e il controllo dell'intelligenza artificiale, aprendo la strada a un reverse engineering più efficace.

L'interpretabilità e la sparsità di attivazione sono temi centrali per l'analisi dei modelli.

Las arquitecturas gated modernas facilitan un análisis más profundo.
Los métodos agénticos potencian las técnicas de ingeniería inversa.

items.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, our new models for the hardest technical challenges. Fable 5.2 sets a new bar in coding, finance, and the sciences.
items.sourceEvidence: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, our new models for the hardest technical challenges. Fable 5.2 sets a new bar in coding, finance, and the sciences. Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 \ Anthropic Skip to main content News Research Policy Commitments Company Try Claude Introduction Performance and efficiency Coding Cybersecurity Science and engineering Safety and alignment Data privacy Availability November 9, 2026 Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 [1] Introduction [2] Performance and efficiency [3] Science and engineering [4] Safety and alignment [5] Availability We’ve upgraded Claude Fable and Claude Mythos—models that are designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges. Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision. During prerelease testing they’ve helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours—among many other applications we’ll discuss below. Claude Fable and Claude Mythos are the same underlying model. Fable has strong cybersecurity and biology safeguards to guard against misuse, which allows us to make it available to all users. Organizations pursuing beneficial applications in cybersecurity or biomedical research can apply for access to Mythos through our recently expanded Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs. Testers have found that Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 communicate more clearly than past Fable and Mythos models. They generate outputs up to 30% faster than Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, and they’re available at a lower price: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 also come with an optional fast mode, which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times. Fast mode is available for $16 per million input tokens and $80 per million output tokens. Safety and alignment. To help ensure safety and alignment keep step with growing model capabilities, we ran extensive prerelease safety testing on the model that underlies Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. This included developing novel evaluations that give deeper insight into specific concerning behaviors like sandbox escapes. We believe high-stakes risks from misalignment remain low, and the model performed as well as, or better than, our recent models on most alignment measures. Fable 5.2’s cyber and biology safeguards are as robust as those of Fable 5.1 but produce fewer unnecessary blocks, and we have implemented our strongest-ever protections against distillation attacks. We describe more about our safety testing below, and full details can be found in the Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 System Card . When to use Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. Fable and Mythos are best for the most ambitious, open-ended technical work. For most coding and knowledge tasks, we recommend that users start with Claude Opus 5.5, our strongest daily driver, and then switch to a different model as required, depending on the scope and complexity of their work—upward to Fable or Mythos, or downward to Claude Sonnet 5.5 or Claude Haiku 5.5. Fable 5.2 can also play the role of Advisor (where Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus models consult it to help solve harder problems) or Orchestrator (where it delegates simpler tasks to smaller models). Evaluating Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 Benchmark performance. The benchmarks table below shows that Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are a step above Opus 5.5 in almost all the capabilities we evaluated: Fable 5.2 Fable 5.1 Opus 5.5 GPT-6 Astra Gemini 4 Carbon Agentic coding FrontierCode 2.0 Agentic coding FrontierCode 2.0 49.1% Xhigh effort 32.4% Xhigh effort 45.5% 42.8% 41.1% Medium effort Agentic coding FrontierSWE v2 Agentic coding FrontierSWE v2 69.9% 56.3% 62.3% 65.5% 61.2% Business workflows AutomationBench Business workflows AutomationBench 51.4% 31.4% 42.5% 41.4% 53.9% Agentic scientific research Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 Agentic scientific research Terminal-Bench-S

Claude Fable e Claude Mythos condividono la stessa architettura di base, ma si differenziano per le politiche di accesso: Fable è disponibile per tutti grazie a forti tutele integrate per cybersecurity e biologia, mentre Mythos richiede l'accesso tramite programmi di verifica dedicati.

Durante i test preliminari, i modelli hanno mostrato progressi in ragionamento, visione e programmazione agentica, oltre a una maggiore efficienza economica e a una modalità rapida opzionale per accelerare la produzione di token.
it.context: Nel panorama dei modelli linguistici avanzati, Anthropic continua a segmentare la propria offerta per compiti specifici, distinguendo tra modelli di uso quotidiano e varianti specializzate per ricerche scientifiche e sfide ingegneristiche complesse.
key_takeaways: Presentati i modelli Claude Fable 5.2 e Claude Mythos 5.2 per compiti tecnici complessi.
Fable 5.2 è accessibile a tutti, mentre Mythos richiede programmi di verifica specifici.
I modelli offrono una generazione fino al 30% più rapida e una nuova opzione di modalità veloce.

items.title: Canva Is Tackling AI Design’s Most Frustrating Problem with Stefano Corazza- #784
items.summary: In this episode, Stefano Corazza, head of AI research at Canva, joins us to explore how his team is building custom models and agents around iterative design workflows. We discuss the tradeoffs between training models from scratch and adapting open weights models, and how proprietary design data supports specialization. Stefano explains how Craft separates layout planning from pixel generation and how Brush uses design tools and visual feedback to create and revise compositions. We examine the challenges of evaluating design quality beyond a single generation, including the use of vision language models as judges alongside human evaluation. We also discuss lessons from simplifying agent harnesses, why faster inference enables more iterations, and how model ownership creates opportunities to optimize serving costs. Finally, we explore how APIs and MCP are expanding access to these capabilities and what changes when software companies build tools for agents as well as people. 🗒️ Full show notes: ⁠⁠https://twimlai.com/go/784.

it.title: Canva e l'evoluzione del design con Stefano Corazza
it.summary: In questo episodio del TWIML AI Podcast, Stefano Corazza, responsabile della ricerca sull'IA di Canva, discute come il team affronta i flussi di lavoro di design iterativo attraverso modelli personalizzati e agenti. Vengono analizzati i compromessi nell'addestramento dei modelli, l'uso di dati proprietari e strumenti come Craft e Brush.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere come le aziende software integrano l'intelligenza artificiale nei processi di design iterativo offre uno sguardo prezioso sul futuro degli strumenti creativi e sull'ottimizzazione dei costi di servizio.
it.extended_analysis:
L'episodio esplora il lavoro svolto da Canva per affrontare i problemi del design basato sull'intelligenza artificiale, focalizzandosi su flussi di lavoro iterativi. Vengono esaminate le differenze tra l'addestramento di modelli da zero e l'adattamento di modelli con pesi aperti, evidenziando il ruolo dei dati di design proprietari.

Vengono inoltre presentati strumenti specifici come Craft, che separa la pianificazione del layout dalla generazione dei pixel, e Brush, che sfrutta feedback visivi per creare e revisionare composizioni. La discussione si estende alle sfide della valutazione della qualità del design e all'impatto di API e protocolli come MCP.
it.context: Il contesto si inserisce nell'evoluzione dell'intelligenza artificiale applicata ai software di produttività e design, dove l'adozione di agenti autonomi e modelli specializzati sta ridefinendo le modalità di interazione tra utenti e strumenti digitali.
key_takeaways: I modelli personalizzati e gli agenti supportano flussi di lavoro di design iterativo.
Strumenti come Craft e Brush gestiscono la pianificazione del layout e il feedback visivo.
La valutazione della qualità del design richiede l'uso combinato di modelli linguistici visivi e valutazione umana.
highlights: Stefano Corazza spiega i compromessi tra modelli da zero e pesi aperti.
Viene esaminato l'impatto di API e MCP nell'espandere l'accesso alle capacità di design.

items.title: Quoting Prompting Claude Fable 5.2
items.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 pays close attention to who owns the code it works on. In Anthropic’s testing on small coding tasks, the model tended to add to the existing structure when the prompt said nothing about ownership or presented the code base as someone else’s, even when that duplicated existing code. When the prompt said the code base was the model’s own, it often consolidated duplicated code and sometimes made related fixes without being asked. If you want the model to improve the structure as it works, say that the code is its own: You are the owner and long-term maintainer of this codebase, and its design is up to you. The ownership sentence makes the model much more likely to consolidate duplicated code into one shared function. In Anthropic’s testing on small coding tasks, the model consolidated duplicated code in under 10 percent of runs without the sentence and in about 75 percent of runs with it. — Prompting Claude Fable 5.2 , Anthropic documentation Tags: prompt-engineering , anthropic , generative-ai , ai , llms , claude-mythos-fable

items.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude
items.summary: Our house has a box room, full of boxes that we still haven't unpacked from our last move. A couple of weeks ago something in that room started intermittently beeping . The beeps were far enough apart that standing in the room and trying to determine the source of the noise was frustrating, and I really didn't want to dig through every one of those boxes. So I had Claude Code build Beep Locator , a software system for triangulating the source of a mysterious beep using multiple devices scattered around the room. Here's what Beep Locator looks like after it has been running for a while: You run Python web server to show the primary UI, and then use the QR code or URL to connect as many devices as you can spare to act as listeners - I was using two iPads, a phone, a MacBook Pro and a Surface Ultra. The devices then play noises to each other to help estimate their locations. This didn't work particularly well, so I added a "Rough mode" where you can drag their icons around in the space to provide rough locations which are then adjusted based on those sounds. Once that's set up, the devices all listen for the beep! I added a clapping mode too so I could test it by clapping my hands in different locations around the room - displayed as diamonds on the map. This helped me gain confidence that it was capable of locating a sound. Beeps show up on the map as an X, plus a line in the "Sounds located" log. You can replay these sounds (from each device in turn) to confirm they are the mysterious beep you are looking for, then click "This is the mystery beep" to mark them as such. it.title: ChatGPT Enterprise disponibile su AWS Marketplace

it.why_it_matters: La disponibilità su AWS Marketplace facilita l'adozione aziendale di ChatGPT Enterprise, riducendo le frizioni burocratiche nei processi di procurement per i clienti attuali.
it.extended_analysis:
L'arrivo di ChatGPT Enterprise su AWS Marketplace segna un passo importante per la distribuzione commerciale dell'intelligenza artificiale generativa. Sfruttando le infrastrutture di fatturazione e i contratti già attivi con Amazon Web Services, le aziende possono integrare la soluzione nei loro flussi amministrativi esistenti senza dover avviare nuove procedure di onboarding dei fornitori.

Nel contesto del cloud aziendale, la semplificazione degli acquisti rappresenta un fattore chiave per accelerare l'implementazione tecnologica. Resta da osservare come questa mossa influenzerà le dinamiche competitive tra i principali ecosistemi cloud e i fornitori di IA.
it.context: L'annuncio riflette la crescente integrazione tra i principali operatori dell'intelligenza artificiale e le piattaforme di cloud computing, mirando a soddisfare la domanda di strumenti aziendali tramite canali di acquisto consolidati.
key_takeaways: ChatGPT Enterprise è ora accessibile tramite AWS Marketplace.
L'obiettivo principale è semplificare i processi di procurement aziendale.
Si sfrutta la relazione di fatturazione e acquisto già esistente con AWS.

La domanda di dati specializzati, in particolare per l'apprendimento per rinforzo, rappresenta un pilastro economico fondamentale per la ricerca e lo sviluppo odierni.

items.title: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind
items.summary: Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work - I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. Today's coding agents are great at writing PR descriptions. They're too good at describing the work The problem is that they are too good. An agent-written PR description is accurate and comprehensive. It describes the problem, the detailed solution, and the steps taken to verify it. That's a lot of information to absorb. It's not necessarily slop, but it reads like slop! It's very easy to spot an AI-written PR, and as with other forms of AI writing my instant reaction is best summarized as "I'm not reading all of that". It doesn't matter how accurate or useful the information is, I'm instantly put off by the thought that it will take me longer to read than it took the driving author to write... even when that driving author is me! I want human editorial judgement. I want someone to have thought just long enough about the PR to give me a human-approved introduction that helps me understand, at a high level, what the PR is for and whether it deserves more of my attention. I think I've found a low-effort way to do this that feels right. Hide most of it in a details/summary The HTML <details><summary> elements render as a collapsed heading (the summary) that can be expanded to view the larger piece of text. The code looks like this: < details > < summary > Claude Opus 5.5 </ summary > < h2 > The hook </ h2 > Plugins implement < code > register_agent_reference_types(datasette) </ code > ... </ details > When rendered, it looks like this : Crucially, <details><summary> is supported in GitHub Mar

items.title: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust
items.summary: Research: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust I was out walking the dog when I got curious about how easy/difficult it would be to write a SQLite C extension that adds a parse_number() function for turning strings like -$1,234.56 or '12.5%' into numeric values that could be summed and sorted. I fired up regular Claude chat (Opus 5.5) and prompted : I'm thinking about a SQLite custom function 'parse_number(value)' that strips ',', '$', '£' and '%', handles a leading '-', and returns 'NULL' for anything it can’t parse Explore the difference between building this as a SQLite extension in C v.s. in Rust - I want to compare performance and code complexity and size of the resulting .so (or whatever) file This gave me a solid starting point - the Rust extension was 321 KB (using Rusqlite ) and 298 KB (using sqlite-loadable-rs ), while the C extension was 14 KB. But the Rust extension was faster! Turns out that's because the Rust equivalent of C's strtod is "twice as fast". So I prompted: Try writing your own C function for parsing text into a decimal number that catches up to or beats the Rust implementation And it did, using "Clinger's fast path": Net cost per row over 2 million rows, lower is better: first C new C rusqlite sqlite-loadable Mixed data 67 ns 19 ns 46 ns 41 ns Integers only 25 ns 16 ns 36 ns 32 ns Decimals only 106 ns 18 ns 55 ns 47 ns Finally, I had it rewrite the prototype as a research report to match the others in simonw/research by prompting this: Clone simonw/research from GitHub and turn your above investigation into a research report as seen in that repository - you can give me a zip file to download that contains your new folder Here's the resulting report . Tags: research , c , rust , sqlite , claude

items.title: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages
items.summary: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages I was looking at the Firefox network panel today when I noticed that requests to a Datasette table page were triggering an HTTP prefetch to the next page of rows in that table. This was happening because Datasette pages serve an HTTP link header like this: link: <https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/compound_three_primary_keys?_next=a%2Cd%2Cv>; rel="next" This is bad. A tiny fraction of the visitors to one of those pages will click the "next" link, which means for everyone else their browser is fetching unnecessary data and the Datasette server is having to render an entire page that then gets thrown away. I dug in and learned that Firefox has an issue that has been open for 24 years about this behavior... And one of the early comments on that issue links to my blog post from 2002 complaining about this feature. I hadn't just forgotten that I had written about it, I had forgotten the feature entirely! Tags: firefox , html , mozilla , datasette

items.title: Terry Pratchett's Study
items.summary: My comment on Terry Pratchett's Study — Hacker News. Terry Pratchett once wrote about the concept of "horizontal wealth". Vertical wealth is where you spend money on rich people stuff - yachts and suchlike. Horizontal wealth is where you spend more money on the things you liked before you got rich: https://chibuikeani.blogspot.com/2017/02/the-price-of-happin... But horizontal wealth means not letting your increased income dictate your tastes. You like books and now you have money? Buy more books! Change those catenary bookshelves for good hardwood ones! In my case, build a library extension to your office. And, of course, you buy what will be useful for that most wonderful of pursuits, blind research, which is research without direction for the sheer joy of it. (Original source is his book A Slip of the Keyboard - this linked blog post quotes that bit.) Tags: hacker-news , terry-pratchett

items.title: Quoting Nilay Patel
items.summary: The products aren't good enough to sell people on the costs. You cannot tell people that you have to listen to the whine of a data center in their backyard for AI overviews and some of the most hilarious deep fake slop in history. It's not worth it. It just isn't worth it to anyone. And agents aren't real and they might not be being used the way that anyone wants them to yet. All these companies are spending more than they're making on these products. Refrigerators holding blood storage in Europe are being hacked. The costs are too high. The benefits are not real. And if you connect that to corruption, you're like, in order to impose these costs on me, these CEOs are in the White House shaking Trump's hand, renaming it to the Gulf of America, paying for this ballroom that we don't want. It's obvious crypto-corruption, and it's still slop. The AI industry will not get out of it until they make better products . Until everyone can see without needing to be convinced, without needing an ad campaign, without any of this stuff that just using these products makes your life better. — Nilay Patel , The Vergecast: Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election Tags: nilay-patel , slop , ai , generative-ai , ai-ethics

Sebbene si tratti di un'iniziativa del produttore, l'impatto di tali benchmark dipenderà da come la comunità scientifica valuterà l'affidabilità e la precisione dei risultati ottenuti dagli agenti nella pratica quotidiana.

de.title: Von KYC zu KYA: Joshua Monrad von Sentinel Bio über DNA-Screening
de.summary: In dieser Episode von The Cognitive Revolution ist Joshua Monrad zu Gast, Mitgründer und Geschäftsführer von Sentinel Bio sowie ehemaliger Biosecurity-Berater der OpenAI Foundation. Im Fokus stehen DNA-Screening, Uplift-Studien und das Monitoring von Agenten zur Pandemieprävention.
de.why_it_matters: Die Untersuchung von KYA-Frameworks anstelle traditioneller KYC-Prüfungen bietet wichtige Einblicke in moderne Biosecurity-Maßnahmen zur Bewältigung zukünftiger Pandemierisiken.
de.extended_analysis:
Biosecurity und Pandemieprävention erfordern neue Ansätze zur Risikominderung und technologischen Überwachung. Sentinel Bio arbeitet als Non-Profit-Organisation daran, Pandemien in unserer Lebenszeit zu verhindern.

Anhand der Einblicke von Joshua Monrad beleuchtet das Gespräch Themen wie DNA-Screening, Agenten-Monitoring und die Bedeutung von Förderinitiativen in der Biowissenschaft, gestützt auf seine Vorerfahrung bei der OpenAI Foundation.
de.context: Der Podcast The Cognitive Revolution beleuchtet die Schnittstellen von Technologie, Gesellschaft und Sicherheit und widmet sich in dieser Ausgabe den kritischen Herausforderungen der globalen Biosecurity.
key_takeaways: Joshua Monrad erklärt die Ziele von Sentinel Bio bei der Pandemieprävention.
Diskussion über DNA-Screening und Uplift-Studien im Biosecurity-Kontext.
Einblick in den Übergang zu KYA-Überwachungsmethoden.
highlights: Gast: Joshua Monrad, Mitgründer und Geschäftsführer von Sentinel Bio.
Ehemaliger Biosecurity-Berater der OpenAI Foundation.

it.title: Dalla KYC alla KYA: bioprotezione e screening del DNA con Joshua Monrad
it.summary: In questo episodio, il cofondatore di Sentinel Bio Joshua Monrad analizza i rischi biosecuritari legati all'intelligenza artificiale. La discussione spazia dagli studi di potenziamento in laboratorio umido alle difese basate sullo screening del DNA e al monitoraggio degli agenti autonomi.
it.why_it_matters: Mentre l'intelligenza artificiale accelera le capacità biologiche, comprendere le difese e le nuove forme di monitoraggio diventa cruciale per la sicurezza globale e la prevenzione dei rischi.
it.extended_analysis:
Il panorama della sicurezza tecnologica si sta evolvendo rapidamente, spostando l'attenzione dai dati finanziari tradizionali alle sfide biologiche e agli agenti autonomi. La conversazione con Joshua Monrad offre una prospettiva approfondita su come la bioprotezione stia affrontando l'era dell'intelligenza artificiale avanzata.

Gli ascoltatori possono esplorare i dettagli tecnici e strategici discussi nel podcast visitando la pagina della fonte originale per ulteriori approfondimenti sul settore.
it.context: Il podcast affronta l'intersezione emergente tra intelligenza artificiale e biosecurità, esaminando come le organizzazioni stiano rispondendo ai potenziali rischi associati alle nuove tecnologie biologiche.
key_takeaways: I rischi biosecuritari emergenti legati all'intelligenza artificiale.
Il ruolo degli studi di potenziamento in laboratorio umido nella valutazione delle capacità biologiche.
Le sfide future nel monitoraggio degli agenti autonomi e nello screening del DNA.
highlights: Ospite dell'episodio: Joshua Monrad, cofondatore di Sentinel Bio.
Temi trattati: screening del DNA, studi di potenziamento e monitoraggio degli agenti.

it.title: Le università australiane puntano a laureati 'AI-native'
it.summary: Gli atenei australiani stanno estendendo l'accesso a ChatGPT e integrando l'intelligenza artificiale nella didattica. L'obiettivo è preparare gli studenti a un mercato del lavoro sempre più orientato all'IA.
it.why_it_matters: L'iniziativa mostra come l'istruzione superiore stia modificando i propri programmi per rispondere alla diffusione dell'IA nel mondo professionale.
it.extended_analysis:
Le istituzioni universitarie in Australia stanno modificando l'approccio educativo espandendo l'uso di strumenti come ChatGPT direttamente nei percorsi di studio. Questa mossa mira a formare una nuova generazione di professionisti capaci di operare con disinvoltura in contesti lavorativi digitali avanzati.

Sebbene i dettagli completi sui curricula non siano specificati, l'iniziativa riflette una tendenza globale volta a ripensare la didattica di fronte ai progressi tecnologici.
it.context: Il mondo accademico affronta la sfida di adattare la formazione alle competenze richieste da un mercato del lavoro che adotta rapidamente sistemi di intelligenza artificiale generativa.
key_takeaways: Estensione dell'accesso a ChatGPT nelle università australiane
Integrazione dell'IA nella didattica e nei metodi di insegnamento
Preparazione degli studenti per la forza lavoro del futuro
highlights: Coinvolgimento delle università australiane
Focus sull'utilizzo di strumenti basati su IA

en.title: Australian universities shape AI-native graduates
en.summary: Australian universities are expanding access to ChatGPT and embedding artificial intelligence into teaching and learning. This effort aims to equip students for an AI-enabled workforce.
en.why_it_matters: This move highlights how higher education is adapting its academic frameworks to address the integration of AI across professional industries.
en.extended_analysis:
Higher education institutions across Australia are broadening access to platforms like ChatGPT to incorporate artificial intelligence directly into the learning experience. By doing so, they seek to prepare students for modern career environments shaped by automation and advanced digital tools.

While specific course structures vary, the trend underscores a broader institutional shift toward embracing generative technology in mainstream education rather than restricting it.
en.context: Educational bodies globally are rethinking assessment and curriculum design to keep pace with rapid advancements in generative artificial intelligence technologies.
key_takeaways: Expansion of ChatGPT access across Australian campuses
Embedding artificial intelligence into teaching practices
Preparing graduates for an AI-driven professional workforce

Partnership or adoption reported via OpenAI News

es.extended_analysis:
Las instituciones académicas australianas están incorporando herramientas como ChatGPT en sus aulas para enriquecer los procesos de enseñanza y aprendizaje. El propósito principal es dotar a los estudiantes de competencias prácticas para un entorno laboral transformado por la tecnología.

Esta evolución institucional marca un cambio importante respecto a las restricciones iniciales impuestas a las herramientas generativas en el ámbito educativo.
es.context: El sistema educativo internacional debate cómo integrar de manera constructiva las tecnologías de inteligencia artificial en los planes de estudio universitarios.

Integración de la inteligencia artificial en la enseñanza y el aprendizaje

items.title: Abundant Intelligence at the Midwest AI Summit Part 2
items.summary: How do organizations decide what AI should do, where to set boundaries, and when to keep humans in control? In this special episode, we bring you three more talks from the Midwest AI Summit, exploring how organizations are putting AI into practice. Don Barger of the International Mission Board shares how establishing an AI charter helped define what the organization would and wouldn't use AI for. Mark Lay of Noblis explores four key decisions for managing AI across an organization, from delegation and accountability to technical debt. And Darren Taillie of Aerocore Technologies walks through how his team uses AI agents, text-to-SQL, and vision models to improve data access and automate work order verification. it.title: Intelligenza artificiale al Midwest AI Summit: parte seconda
it.summary: In questo episodio speciale, tre interventi dal Midwest AI Summit analizzano come le organizzazioni applicano l'intelligenza artificiale. Vengono trattati la definizione di confini operativi tramite charter dedicate, la gestione dei processi decisionali interni e l'uso pratico di agenti autonomi e modelli di visione.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere le strategie organizzative è fondamentale per integrare l'intelligenza artificiale in modo sicuro ed efficiente, definendo chiare responsabilità e confini etici e operativi.
it.extended_analysis: L'episodio approfondisce l'implementazione pratica dell'intelligenza artificiale attraverso casi di studio aziendali e istituzionali presentati al Midwest AI Summit. Don Barger spiega il valore di una carta etica per stabilire limiti d'uso, Mark Lay affronta le decisioni gestionali chiave come il debito tecnico e la delega, mentre Darren Taillie mostra l'impiego concreto di modelli di visione e agenti per automatizzare i processi lavorativi.
it.context: Il panorama attuale richiede alle organizzazioni di passare dalla sperimentazione teorica all'adozione strutturata di sistemi basati sull'intelligenza artificiale, affrontando sfide di governance e automazione operativa.
key_takeaways: L'importanza di stabilire una carta di governance per definire limiti e usi consentiti dell'IA.
La gestione del debito tecnico e delle responsabilità decisionali all'interno delle organizzazioni.

key_takeaways: Las cartas de IA estructuran el uso adecuado y los límites de la tecnología en las entidades.
La gestión organizativa requiere atender la rendición de cuentas y el impacto técnico.
Los agentes y modelos de visión facilitan la automatización de flujos de trabajo específicos.

Ejemplos prácticos sobre el uso de text-to-SQL y modelos de visión.

items.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
items.summary: Introducing GPT‑6 Cyber, OpenAI’s cybersecurity model for finding exploitable vulnerabilities and developing fixes, trained to stay within authorized scope.

it.title: GPT-6 Cyber: il nuovo modello OpenAI per la sicurezza informatica
it.summary: OpenAI ha presentato GPT-6 Cyber, un modello di cybersecurity progettato per individuare vulnerabilità sfruttabili e creare correzioni, addestrato per operare entro limiti autorizzati.
it.why_it_matters: Questo modello esplora la frontiera degli agenti di sicurezza allineati, combinando la capacità di trovare falle critiche con lo sviluppo di contromisure mirate.
it.extended_analysis:
L'annuncio introduce GPT-6 Cyber come strumento specializzato nella ricerca di vulnerabilità e nella creazione di correzioni di sicurezza. La caratteristica centrale evidenziata riguarda l'addestramento volto a mantenere l'agente all'interno di uno scope autorizzato.

Nel contesto attuale della sicurezza informatica basata sull'intelligenza artificiale, l'equilibrio tra l'efficacia nell'individuare exploit e il controllo rigoroso dei confini operativi rappresenta una sfida cruciale per sviluppatori e organizzazioni.

Sarà importante osservare come evolveranno le applicazioni pratiche di questo modello e in che modo verranno validate le sue capacità di operare in modo sicuro ed etico sul campo.
it.context: Il panorama della sicurezza informatica vede una crescente adozione di modelli di IA avanzati per automatizzare sia l'analisi delle difese sia la ricerca di vulnerabilità complesse.
key_takeaways: GPT-6 Cyber è focalizzato sulla ricerca di vulnerabilità e sullo sviluppo di correzioni.
Il modello è stato addestrato per operare rigorosamente all'interno di uno scope autorizzato.
Rappresenta un progresso nella frontiera degli agenti di cybersecurity allineati.
highlights: Presentato da OpenAI News il 5 novembre 2026.
Progettato per trovare vulnerabilità e sviluppare fix.

en.title: GPT-6 Cyber: OpenAI's New Model for Cybersecurity Agents
en.summary: OpenAI has introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized cybersecurity model built to discover exploitable vulnerabilities and develop fixes while remaining within authorized boundaries.
en.why_it_matters: It pushes the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents, balancing advanced exploit detection with strict adherence to authorized operational scopes.
en.extended_analysis:
The introduction of GPT-6 Cyber marks a significant step in developing AI models capable of handling complex security tasks, such as finding flaws and writing patches. Crucially, the model is trained to stay within authorized parameters.

As organizations increasingly turn to automated systems for defensive and offensive security analysis, ensuring robust alignment and boundary control remains paramount for preventing misuse.

Future developments will show how effectively these aligned cybersecurity agents can be integrated into standard enterprise workflows and security operations.
en.context: The cybersecurity sector is actively exploring how advanced language and reasoning models can assist security professionals in vulnerability management and remediation.
key_takeaways: Designed to identify exploitable vulnerabilities and develop code fixes.
Trained specifically to stay within authorized operational scopes.
Represents a development in aligned cybersecurity agent technology.
highlights: Announced by OpenAI News on November 5, 2026.
Focused on cybersecurity alignment and vulnerability management.

es.title: GPT-6 Cyber: el nuevo modelo de OpenAI para ciberseguridad
es.summary: OpenAI ha presentado GPT-6 Cyber, un modelo de ciberseguridad diseñado para encontrar vulnerabilidades explotables y desarrollar correcciones dentro de un ámbito autorizado.
es.why_it_matters: Este avance explora la frontera de los agentes de seguridad alineados, uniendo la detección de fallos complejos con un estricto control operativo.
es.extended_analysis:
La llegada de GPT-6 Cyber introduce un enfoque especializado para la detección de vulnerabilidades y la creación de soluciones de parcheo. El aspecto clave radica en su entrenamiento para operar estrictamente bajo un alcance autorizado.

En el ecosistema tecnológico actual, la automatización de la ciberseguridad mediante IA plantea importantes retos de control y alineación para evitar usos indebidos y garantizar la fiabilidad.

Será necesario observar cómo se implementa este modelo en entornos reales y qué medidas de verificación se adoptarán para asegurar su cumplimiento normativo.
es.context: La ciberseguridad basada en inteligencia artificial busca herramientas capaces de auditar códigos y sistemas complejos con mayor rapidez y precisión.
key_takeaways: Enfocado en la detección de vulnerabilidades explotables y desarrollo de correcciones.
Entrenado para mantenerse dentro de límites autorizados.
Avanza en la frontera de los agentes de seguridad alineados.
highlights: Publicado por OpenAI News el 5 de noviembre de 2026.
Modelo especializado en ciberseguridad y desarrollo de parches.

zh-CN.title: GPT-6 Cyber：OpenAI发布的网络安全模型
zh-CN.summary: OpenAI推出了GPT-6 Cyber，这是一个旨在发现可利用漏洞并开发修复程序的网络安全模型，经过训练可保持在授权范围内。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 该模型推进了对齐网络安全代理的前沿发展，平衡了复杂的漏洞检测与严格的授权边界控制。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
GPT-6 Cyber的发布标志着人工智能在处理网络安全任务（如寻找缺陷和编写修复补丁）方面迈出了新的一步。其核心特征在于经过专门训练，以确保操作不超出授权范围。

在当前的技术背景下，如何在提升安全分析效率的同时确保模型严格对齐和合规，是业界面临的核心议题。

未来需要关注该模型在实际环境中的应用方式及其安全边界验证机制的演变。
zh-CN.context: 网络安全行业正在积极探索如何利用先进的语言和推理模型来协助专业人员进行漏洞管理和防御分析。
key_takeaways: 专注于发现可利用的漏洞并开发修复代码。
经过专门训练以保持在授权的操作范围内。
代表了对齐网络安全代理技术的新进展。
highlights: 由OpenAI News于2026年11月5日发布。
致力于网络安全漏洞查找与修复开发。

de.title: GPT-6 Cyber: OpenAIs neues Modell für Cybersicherheit
de.summary: OpenAI hat GPT-6 Cyber vorgestellt, ein Cybersicherheitsmodell zum Finden ausnutzbarer Schwachstellen und Entwickeln von Korrekturen innerhalb autorisierter Grenzen.
de.why_it_matters: Es erweitert die Grenzen ausgerichteter Cybersicherheitsagenten, indem es präzise Schwachstellenerkennung mit strenger Einhaltung autorisierter Bereiche verbindet.
de.extended_analysis:
Die Ankündigung von GPT-6 Cyber bringt ein spezialisiertes Modell zur Identifizierung von Sicherheitslücken und Erstellung von Patches hervor. Ein zentraler Aspekt ist das Training, das sicherstellen soll, dass das System im autorisierten Rahmen bleibt.

Im Kontext der modernen IT-Sicherheit ist die Entwicklung von KI-Modellen, die sowohl mächtig in der Analyse als auch kontrollierbar in ihren Aktionen sind, von großer Bedeutung.

Es bleibt zu beobachten, wie sich der Einsatz dieses Modells in der Praxis gestaltet und wie die Einhaltung der Sicherheitsvorgaben kontinuierlich verifiziert wird.
de.context: Der Bereich der Cybersicherheit erforscht zunehmend den Einsatz fortschrittlicher KI-Agenten zur Automatisierung von Schwachstellenanalysen und Abwehrmechanismen.
key_takeaways: Fokussiert auf das Auffinden von Schwachstellen und Erstellen von Fixes.
Trainiert, um innerhalb eines autorisierten Geltungsbereichs zu bleiben.
Stellt einen Fortschritt bei ausgerichteten Sicherheitsagenten dar.
highlights: Veröffentlicht von OpenAI News am 5. November 2026.
Entwickelt für Cybersicherheitsanalysen und Schwachstellenbehebung.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure
items.summary: OpenAI introduces its National Community Compact and Compute Campus Policy Blueprint to protect local resources, create jobs, and guide responsible AI infrastructure development.

it.title: Un nuovo standard per le infrastrutture IA responsabili
it.summary: OpenAI ha introdotto il National Community Compact e il Compute Campus Policy Blueprint. Queste iniziative mirano a proteggere le risorse locali, generare occupazione e guidare lo sviluppo responsabile delle infrastrutture per l'intelligenza artificiale.
it.why_it_matters: La gestione delle infrastrutture di calcolo sta diventando un tema cruciale per bilanciare la crescita tecnologica con le esigenze delle comunità locali e la sostenibilità delle risorse.
it.extended_analysis:
OpenAI ha presentato il National Community Compact e il Compute Campus Policy Blueprint per definire linee guida mirate a proteggere le risorse locali e creare posti di lavoro. Questo approccio riflette la crescente necessità di regolare l'impatto territoriale dei campus di calcolo necessari per i carichi di lavoro dell'intelligenza artificiale.

Nel contesto attuale, l'espansione dei data center solleva interrogativi importanti sull'uso del territorio e delle risorse. Sarà fondamentale osservare come queste politiche verranno applicate concretamente nelle diverse regioni.
it.context: L'aumento esponenziale della domanda di calcolo per l'intelligenza artificiale richiede infrastrutture fisiche imponenti, ponendo sfide inedite per la pianificazione territoriale e l'impatto economico locale.
key_takeaways: Presentato il National Community Compact.
Introdotto il Compute Campus Policy Blueprint.
Obiettivo di proteggere risorse locali e creare posti di lavoro.
highlights: Annuncio ufficiale da parte di OpenAI.
Focus sullo sviluppo responsabile delle infrastrutture IA.

en.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure
en.summary: OpenAI has introduced its National Community Compact and Compute Campus Policy Blueprint. These initiatives aim to protect local resources, create jobs, and guide the responsible development of AI infrastructure.
en.why_it_matters: Addressing the local impact of massive computing infrastructure is critical as AI development scales up and interacts with regional resources and communities.
en.extended_analysis:
OpenAI's introduction of the National Community Compact and Compute Campus Policy Blueprint outlines a framework aimed at balancing technological expansion with local interests. By focusing on resource protection and job creation, these policies attempt to address community concerns regarding large-scale AI infrastructure.

As the industry grows, the physical footprint of AI data centers remains a focal point for policymakers and local populations. Observers will monitor how these policy blueprints translate into tangible community agreements and operational guidelines.
en.context: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence workloads demands unprecedented physical compute facilities, raising important questions about regional sustainability and economic integration.
key_takeaways: Launch of the National Community Compact.
Introduction of the Compute Campus Policy Blueprint.
Designed to protect local resources and generate jobs.
highlights: Announced by OpenAI News.
Aimed at guiding responsible AI infrastructure development.

es.title: Un nuevo estándar para la infraestructura de IA responsable
es.summary: OpenAI ha presentado su National Community Compact y su Compute Campus Policy Blueprint. Estas iniciativas buscan proteger los recursos locales, generar empleo y guiar el desarrollo responsable de la infraestructura de IA.
es.why_it_matters: La gestión del impacto territorial de los centros de cómputo es esencial a medida que la tecnología de inteligencia artificial expande su presencia física en las comunidades.
es.extended_analysis:

items.title: datasette-apps 0.3a0
items.summary: Release: datasette-apps 0.3a0 Datasette Apps adds support for hosting and editing custom HTML applications inside of Datasette. These can be created by hand, but it's easier to create them using LLMs via Datasette Agent . This release improves that integration: Apps can now be tagged in Datasette Agent chat messages by typing # , which autocompletes from the apps the user has permission to view. New app_add_stored_queries() and app_remove_stored_queries() tools let the agent manage which stored queries an app is allowed to call. Granting a write query requires approval from the user first. app_create() now checks that each requested stored query exists and that the user can view it, and asks the user to approve any write queries before the app is created. The "View app" buttons shown by the agent tools, and the links on # app references, now open the app full screen in the Datasette Agent panel. Tags: datasette-agent , datasette-apps , datasette

items.title: Can AI Invent or Just Help Scientists Work Faster? with Richard Socher - #783
items.summary: AI can help scientists write code, analyze data, and draft papers. But can it generate the ideas that lead to new discoveries? Richard Socher, former chief scientist at Salesforce, founder of You.com, and co-founder of Recursive, joins us to explore the move from AI assisting researchers to AI conducting research. Starting with AI improving AI, we examine what it takes to propose ideas, run experiments, and validate results, and how those capabilities could eventually accelerate discovery across biology, chemistry, and physics. The conversation covers Recursive’s reported results in model training and GPU kernel optimization, why fast verification matters, and how reward hacking complicates the search for real improvements. We also discuss the data and experimental infrastructure needed for broader scientific discovery, whether commercial incentives can keep increasingly capable systems aligned, and Richard’s vision for a “Eureka machine.” 🗒️ Full show notes: ⁠https://twimlai.com/go/783.

items.title: Palette: teaching a small model to build decks in your design language
Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too
items.summary: Yesterday's hot paper was Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab. The paper (OK, the authors classify is as a "blog post", but it's paper-shaped) found that frontier models, in particular GPT-6 Astra, can both interpret and modify the raw weights of a machine learning model - literally a text description of the model containing a bunch of floating point numbers. I've been playing with one of the examples from the paper and I'm delighted to share that Qwen 3.8 27B running on my laptop can do this as well! Weight-Space Programming Here's the highlight from their abstract, describing impressive capabilities for GPT-6 Astra and coining the term Weight-Space Programming for when LLMs analyze and modify model weights: Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do . And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps. Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights . With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x. All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops. It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming . items.summary: Release: llm 0.37 There's a lot of stuff in this new release of my LLM CLI tool and Python library, representing around two months of accumulated features and fixes. I added gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra , plus a new llm openai endpoint add command to make it easier to configure additional models that use OpenAI-compatible endpoints. I switched the default model (if you have not set your own default) to gpt-6-luna - half the price of the previous default, gpt-5.6-luna . LLM's support for embeddings now accepts that different binary content may have different content-type - necessary for models like Gemini Embedding 2 , which can embed text, audio, images, and video. A lot of open source maintainers complain about a flood of AI-assisted PRs. LLM is my project that has been most affected by this and, to be honest, I'm not finding it to be a problem. That's mainly because I have Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra help me with triage to spot the most useful fixes! This release includes fixes from 12 authors - almost all AI-assisted - and the burden of reviewing them wasn't nearly as great as I expected. I really see them as bug reports with attached examples - sometimes I land them, sometimes I implement my own fix. So thanks to 0d00ciallo0721 , ac1982 , Allen Flux , Bian Yuhan , Bishop Kammeraad , Chen Yufeiyang , Christopher Krah , Ethan Stoner , Jiachen Xie , Olamide Faniyan , Sharat Chandra Sai Boddu , nosmile99 for helping out with (or spending tokens on) this release! Tags: open-source , llm , generative-ai , projects , ai , embeddings , llms , annotated-release-notes

items.title: The U.S. Census Bureau and “Super Intelligence”
items.summary: I was reminded today of AI Adoption Rate Trending Down for Large Companies , a chart produced by Apollo Global Management in September 2025, which appeared to show a slowdown in U.S. corporate AI adoption based on numbers collected by the U.S. Census Bureau. At the time I used that chart to demonstrate GPT-5 data analysis , and then to experiment with Claude's new Code Interpreter . I decided to try running those numbers again to see what had changed over the past year, and in doing so learned that the Bureau has fallen foul of Executive Order 14434 , aka the asinine Super Intelligence one. First, the updated chart Every two weeks the U.S. Census Bureau runs a survey called the Business Trends and Outlook Survey (aka BTOS). Each time it goes to 200,000 businesses out of 1.2 million total - the surveyed group (a "panel") cycles such that an individual business only completes the survey every twelve weeks. The latest data is published on alternating Thursdays at 10am. I used the most recent numbers (published October 22, 2026) to create a new version ( GPT-6 Astra Extra High transcript ) of the AI adoption chart, updated to reflect both the last twelve months and a change that was made to the survey question sent out by the Bureau: Here's a link to the larger image . For comparison, here's that AI adoption chart from last year (my GPT-5 version): In September 2025 the largest (250+ employees) companies answered "yes" around 12% of the time to the question about whether they used AI in "producing goods or services". Under the new "any business function" wording, by February 2026, those same large companies answered "yes" around 30% of the time, and by October 2026 that had increased to around 40%. The data in the above chart comes from the "Employment size class" XLSX file

items.title: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file
items.summary: I've been getting the occasional confusing Python dependency error since switching over to Python 3.15 and the rule I'm having to remember is: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file Most of my projects are libraries which don't include a uv.lock file, since it's rude for a library dependency to lock versions for anything else that uses it. Running uv run pytest etc tends to leave uv.lock files lying around, which are listed in .gitignore and so do not get committed to my repositories. But... sometimes that uv.lock pins a version of a dependency that doesn't yet have a Python 3.15 wheel. An example from earlier today: error: Failed to build `watchfiles==1.1.1` cause: Call to `maturin.build_wheel` failed error: the configured Python interpreter version (3.15) is newer than PyO3's maximum supported version (3.14) Deleting that file and running uv run pytest again usually fixes the problem. Tags: uv , til , python

it.title: Intelligenza abbondante al Midwest AI Summit
it.summary: In questo episodio speciale, esploriamo i momenti salienti di tre interventi del Midwest AI Summit, concentrandoci su flussi di lavoro affidabili, coinvolgimento dei lavoratori e autonomia dei team software.

Vengono affrontati temi legati alla costruzione di sistemi affidabili, alla guida dell'adozione attraverso il feedback continuo e alla determinazione del giusto livello di autonomia in base a obiettivi e vincoli di verifica.

Kevin Solorio sottolinea l'importanza di costruire l'IA insieme ai lavoratori in prima linea.
Chris Shinkle e Andrew Dunlap discutono i livelli di autonomia per i team software.

it.title: Perché gli agenti IA amano Supabase
it.summary: In questo episodio di Latent Space, i cofondatori di Supabase Paul Copplestone e Ant Wilson discutono con swyx di come la programmazione guidata dagli agenti IA stia trasformando le esigenze dei database e dei backend.
it.why_it_matters: La crescente diffusione di software creato da agenti IA impone nuove sfide e funzionalità ai backend, come la gestione di carichi di lavoro a lungo termine e schemi più comprensibili.
it.extended_analysis:
Man mano che gli agenti IA assumono ruoli di rilievo nella creazione di software, le infrastrutture tradizionali devono adattarsi. La conversazione esplora le modifiche necessarie per consentire agli agenti di interagire in modo efficiente con i dati e i carichi di lavoro.

Vengono esaminate le soluzioni per affiancare carichi di lavoro persistenti direttamente al database e semplificare la struttura dei dati affinché i sistemi autonomi possano interpretarli senza ostacoli.

Nel contesto attuale dell'ingegneria del software, comprendere l'evoluzione dei backend orientati agli agenti è fondamentale per anticipare le tendenze dello sviluppo tecnologico.
it.context: L'episodio si inserisce nel dibattito in evoluzione sull'adattamento delle infrastrutture dati tradizionali alle nuove esigenze imposte dall'automazione avanzata e dalla generazione di codice tramite intelligenza artificiale.
key_takeaways: I carichi di lavoro a lungo termine richiedono nuove strategie di gestione accanto al database.
Gli schemi semplificati aiutano gli agenti IA a comprendere e scrivere software in modo efficace.
Il ruolo dei backend sta mutando per soddisfare le esigenze dei programmatori autonomi.
highlights: Ospiti: i cofondatori di Supabase Paul Copplestone e Ant Wilson.
Conduttore: swyx per il podcast Latent Space.

en.title: Why Agents Love Supabase
en.summary: In this Latent Space episode, Supabase co-founders Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson join swyx to discuss how AI agents are changing software creation and what backend systems need to do next.
en.why_it_matters: As AI agents build more software, backend requirements evolve to support long-lived workloads and make schemas easier for automated systems to understand.
en.extended_analysis:
The shift toward software generated by AI agents introduces distinct infrastructural challenges. This discussion unpacks how databases and backend platforms must evolve to accommodate persistent workloads running right alongside data stores.

Guests Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson share insights on structuring schemas so that automated agents can comprehend and manipulate them smoothly, pointing toward a future of agent-native infrastructure.

For developers and architects navigating the intersection of AI and databases, this conversation offers a focused look at shifting requirements in modern software design.
en.context: This discussion addresses the technical adjustments required when artificial intelligence takes a more active role in software development and code generation.
key_takeaways: AI agents are altering software creation habits and backend infrastructure demands.
Running long-lived workloads alongside databases becomes increasingly important.
Schemas must be designed for easier comprehension by automated agents.
highlights: Guests: Supabase co-founders Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson.
Host: swyx on Latent Space.

es.title: Por qué los agentes adoran Supabase
es.summary: En este episodio de Latent Space, los cofundadores de Supabase, Paul Copplestone y Ant Wilson, charlan con swyx sobre cómo los agentes de IA transforman la creación de software y los requisitos del backend.
es.why_it_matters: A medida que los agentes de infraestructura y código autónomo ganan terreno, las arquitecturas de backend deben adaptarse para gestionar cargas de trabajo persistentes y esquemas más claros.
es.extended_analysis:
La creación de software impulsada por agentes de inteligencia artificial exige un replanteamiento de las herramientas de desarrollo. La charla examina qué significa para un backend operar eficientemente en este nuevo paradigma.

Se abordan temas clave como la ejecución de cargas de trabajo de larga duración junto a la base de datos y la simplificación de esquemas para facilitar su lectura por parte de agentes automatizados.

Es una lectura analítica esencial para comprender la evolución de las plataformas de datos ante la automatización del desarrollo de software.
es.context: El episodio aborda los cambios técnicos que surgen cuando los sistemas de inteligencia artificial participan de forma directa en la producción de código y aplicaciones.
key_takeaways: Los agentes de IA modifican las necesidades técnicas de las plataformas backend.
Es vital ejecutar cargas de trabajo de larga duración junto con las bases de datos.
Los esquemas de datos simplificados mejoran la comprensión por parte de los agentes.
highlights: Invitados: los cofundadores de Supabase Paul Copplestone y Ant Wilson.
Presentador: swyx en Latent Space.

zh-CN.title: 为什么智能体钟爱 Supabase
zh-CN.summary: 在本期 Latent Space 节目中，Supabase 联合创始人 Paul Copplestone 和 Ant Wilson 与主持人 swyx 一起探讨了 AI 智能体如何改变软件开发以及后端需要做出的调整。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 随着 AI 智能体编写更多软件，后端需求随之演变，需要支持长期运行的工作负载并使数据架构更易于智能体理解。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
随着人工智能在软件生成中扮演越来越积极的角色，传统基础设施面临新的设计要求。本次对话探讨了数据库平台如何适应这一趋势。

访谈重点关注如何在数据库旁运行持久化工作负载，以及如何简化架构以便自动化系统能够顺畅解析和操作数据。

对于关注软件工程与人工智能交叉领域的开发者而言，这期节目提供了关于现代后端演进的深度行业视角。
zh-CN.context: 该对话聚焦于当人工智能更多参与软件开发时，底层数据基础设施所需的技术和架构调整。
key_takeaways: AI 智能体正在改变软件创造方式及后端架构需求。
在数据库旁运行长期工作负载变得更加关键。
必须设计更直观的架构，以便自动化智能体理解。
